title: Normalized cohomology coefficient comparisons
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a coefficient datum C, a simultaneous normalized operations family S as in [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-data], a separated finite-type geometric space X over the algebraically closed field of D, and a compactification c of its structure map. There exist point scalar unitors and point scalar composition isomorphisms normalized on K-flat cochains, and a family u(f,compact) of natural isomorphisms from cohomology at the source stage followed by point scalar extension to site scalar extension followed by cohomology at the target stage. The family satisfies RingedCohomologyNormalized, LocalizationCohomologyNormalized and FieldCohomologyNormalized, for the exact maps in [def-sf-mixed-cup-ringed-normalization] and [def-sf-mixed-cup-field-normalization]. Its identity component is the point unitor, and its component on a formal composite is the point associator, followed by the scalar image of the first comparison, followed by the second comparison. No site tensor comparison and no cup square is asserted.

proof.text:
For finite coefficients use the ordinary counit-transpose scalar mate and
its invertibility on finite-Tor etale-origin inputs. For support use the proper
scalar comparison followed by the open balancing isomorphism, and transport the
etale construction through the canonical site comparison. For integral reduction
use the operation reduction maps; for integral extension use the finite-free
completed scalar comparison. Its ordinary direct-image mate is invertible: after
restriction and a finite basis it is the finite direct sum of the old direct
image. Restriction reflects invertibility. These are checks of the canonical
maps, so they do not introduce a basis choice. Conjugate by the actual operation
coordinates, apply exact point sections and the prescribed scalar/sections map.
Rationalize the integral comparisons, then represent closure comparisons over a
common finite field. Their naturality gives natural isomorphisms. Define the
identity component by the normalized point unitor, and define the component of
a formal composite by the displayed three-map composite. The elementary
normalization predicates then hold by construction. The point unitor and
associator descend from ordinary scalar balancing on K-flat complexes; scalar
extension preserves K-flatness. Their universal counit equations give the two
point normalization predicates. This proves the displayed identity and formal
composition laws without asserting a new cup square.

lean.statement: theorem operationComparisons_exists (S : Operations C) (X : SixFunctorSpace D) [IsSeparated X.obj.hom] (c : Compactification (sixFunctorStructure X).hom.left) : ∃ pointUnit : ∀ a : Stage C, pointChange C (.identity a) ≅ 𝟭 _, ∃ pointComp : ∀ {a b d : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) (g : Passage C b d), pointChange C (.comp f g) ≅ pointChange C f ⋙ pointChange C g, ∃ cohomologyIso : ∀ {a b : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) (compact : Bool), cohomology C S X c compact a ⋙ pointChange C f ≅ change C X f ⋙ cohomology C S X c compact b, (∀ a, PointUnitNormalized C a (pointUnit a)) ∧ (∀ {a b d : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) (g : Passage C b d), PointCompNormalized C f g (pointComp f g)) ∧ (RingedCohomologyNormalized C S X c cohomologyIso) ∧ (LocalizationCohomologyNormalized C S X c cohomologyIso) ∧ (FieldCohomologyNormalized C S X c cohomologyIso) ∧ (∀ (a : Stage C) (compact : Bool) (K : (domain C X.obj.left a).FullSubcategory), (cohomologyIso (.identity a) compact).hom.app K = (pointUnit a).hom.app ((cohomology C S X c compact a).obj K)) ∧ (∀ {a b d : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) (g : Passage C b d) (compact : Bool) (K : (domain C X.obj.left a).FullSubcategory), (cohomologyIso (.comp f g) compact).hom.app K = (pointComp f g).hom.app ((cohomology C S X c compact a).obj K) ≫ (pointChange C g).map ((cohomologyIso f compact).hom.app K) ≫ (cohomologyIso g compact).hom.app ((change C X f).obj K))
